_about: TornadoC2 agent build configuration — complete field reference
_version: matches the transport, profile, and injection schema documented in README.md
_description: Loaded by BeaconHandler._load_build_config() on the team server.
Every field is optional. Missing values fall back to the named
opsec_profile. Keys beginning with '_' are comments and are ignored
by the loader, so this file is safe to hand to an operator as-is.
This file is a reference, not a working build. Copy a recipe from
the '_recipes' block below into a new file, edit the values you
need, and pass it to the builder. Every recipe is a complete,
_recipes_doc: Each recipe below is a complete, valid config on its own. Copy one, edit the values you need, save it as a new file, and pass that file to beacon-build or build. The placeholders REPLACE_WITH_* must be filled in before the build will succeed.

plain_http_linux._comment: Baseline Linux HTTPS beacon. The simplest build that reaches a real handler.

plain_http_windows._comment: Baseline Windows HTTPS beacon. Pair the C2 profile with a matching TLS profile — a profile that claims Chrome while the ClientHello is the Go standard library is a two-signal mismatch. This recipe uses the chrome profile on both layers so the UA and the ClientHello agree. If you want a service-specific C2 profile such as slack, the tls_profile should still be chrome because Slack's own client uses a Chrome-shaped ClientHello — a slack UA over a Go ClientHello is a mismatch, and a slack UA over a Chrome ClientHello is consistent.

https_dns_failover._comment: HTTPS primary, rotate to DNS TXT after N consecutive transport failures. Rotation is a ring, not a preference list: once the agent rotates it stays on the new transport until that one also fails N times.

https_doh_failover._comment: HTTPS primary, rotate to DNS-over-HTTPS. Reaches networks that filter UDP/53 but permit HTTPS to a public resolver. The C2 must still run the DNS transport — the public resolver forwards to the C2's authoritative NS on UDP/53.

dns_only._comment: UDP DNS TXT only. Optionally add "c2_profile": "dns" to rename the three DNS verb characters and shrink the per-chunk payload length. Both sides must name the same profile — the agent reads the block through the builder's linker flags, and the listener reads it through --beacon-profile. A build with c2_profile 'dns' against a handler started without --beacon-profile will work only if the handler's alphabetical scan happens to pick the same block, which is not guaranteed. Run a DNS engagement with --beacon-profile dns on the listener.

doh_only._comment: DoH only. Blends with browser DoH; the resolver-to-C2 hop is still unencrypted UDP/53. The tls_profile matters here — the ClientHello to the public resolver is exactly the fingerprint that determines whether the traffic looks like a browser or a Go client.

quic_only._comment: QUIC / HTTP/3 only. The url port must match the handler's --beacon-quic-port. tls_profile is accepted but ignored — QUIC composes its own TLS 1.3 ClientHello and Go's QUIC stack does not accept a uTLS dialer. Requires aioquic on the server and quic-go in the agent's go.mod. Cannot be combined with another transport in this version.

websocket_only._comment: WebSocket over TLS only. The url port must match the handler's --ws-port, NOT --beacon-port. The client converts https:// to wss:// at dial time, so the same value works for HTTP and WebSocket builds. tls_profile applies — the WebSocket handshake is a real TLS handshake. Requires simple-websocket on the server and coder/websocket in the agent's go.mod. mTLS is not supported on this transport. Cannot be combined with another transport in this version.

wireguard_only._comment: WireGuard-only build. Copy the server's WireGuard public key from the handler's startup banner. Generate the agent keypair on the team server with `wg genkey | tee agent.key | wg pubkey`; paste the private half below, and pin the public half server-side after deployment with `wireguard add-peer <pubkey> 10.99.0.2`. Until the pin is in place, WireGuard silently drops the agent's packets — there is no server-side log line for an unpinned peer. wireguard_inner_port must match the handler's --beacon-port. wireguard_server_tunnel_ip must match the handler's --wireguard-server-ip. Requires pyroute2, the wireguard kernel module, and CAP_NET_ADMIN on the server; requires chrj/wgnet in the agent's go.mod. Cannot be combined with another transport in this version.

icmp_only._comment: ICMP echo only. Linux-only on both sides. Requires CAP_NET_RAW on the Python process on the C2 host — either run the handler as root, or `setcap cap_net_raw+ep $(which python3)`. icmp_host is the C2's public IPv4 address as reachable from the target, and is obfuscated in the compiled binary. ICMP has a ~1400-byte per-reply data-field cap; it is not the transport for file transfer or large BOF delivery.

smb_parent._comment: SMB pivot listener. Carries child traffic over its own HTTP transport. Deploy this before the SMB child. Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path. The parent polls 24/7 so it is always available to relay child traffic — the work_hours fields are set to 00:00/00:00 for that reason, and kill_days is 0 for the same reason: a parent that self-destructs mid-engagement orphans every child behind it. WARNING: kill_days=0 means the agent has NO self-destruct deadline and NO automatic cleanup. An operator who forgets to issue `kill` on a parent at the end of an engagement leaves a live beacon on the network indefinitely. On a monitored network, 24/7 polling is itself a fingerprint; a parent that polls outside business hours stands out. Requires Donut on the build host if inject is enabled.

smb_child._comment: SMB pivot child, CROSS-HOST form. Dials the parent's named pipe over SMB. The smb_pipe value is the parent's UNC path — the parent's hostname (or IP), then \pipe\, then the pipe name the parent was built with. Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path. Requires TCP/445 reachability from the child to the parent, and a child process token that can authenticate to the parent's host. Wire encryption (server_ecdh_pubkey_b64) IS supported on a pivot child — the child's C2 body travels inside the pivot tunnel and the parent carries it opaquely. On bash, single-quote the smb_pipe value so the shell does not collapse the leading backslashes.

smb_child_local._comment: SMB pivot child, SAME-HOST form. Dials the parent's pipe as a local pipe. The child and parent must run on the same Windows host — this is a privilege-separation pivot, not a network pivot. Use this when the child's process token cannot reach the team server directly (different session, lower-privilege service account, or a process whose egress is blocked by policy) but the parent can. Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path. The smb_pipe value is the same bare name the parent was built with — no UNC prefix, no hostname.

tcp_parent._comment: TCP pivot listener. Dials the TCP child's listener and relays its traffic over the parent's HTTP transport. The tcp_relay_token must match the child's tcp_bind_token. The parent polls 24/7 so it is always available to relay. Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path. WARNING: kill_days=0 means the agent has NO self-destruct deadline and NO automatic cleanup. An operator who forgets to issue `kill` on a parent at the end of an engagement leaves a live beacon on the network indefinitely. On a monitored network, 24/7 polling is itself a fingerprint.

tcp_child._comment: TCP pivot child. Opens a TCP listener and waits for the parent to dial. Generate a token with `beacon-build --tcp-token-gen` or `python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))'`. The token must be 64 hex characters (32 bytes). Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path.

tcp_rev_parent._comment: TCP reverse pivot listener. The parent opens a TCP listener that a tcprev child dials. Build this FIRST — it generates the token the child needs. The token must be 64 hex characters (32 bytes); both ends must carry the same value. The parent polls 24/7 so it is always available to relay, and kill_days is 0 for the same reason: a parent that self-destructs mid-engagement orphans every child behind it. WARNING: kill_days=0 means the agent has NO self-destruct deadline and NO automatic cleanup. An operator who forgets to issue `kill` on a parent at the end of an engagement leaves a live beacon on the network indefinitely. On a monitored network, 24/7 polling is itself a fingerprint.

tcp_rev_child._comment: TCP reverse pivot child. Dials the parent's listener; the parent does NOT dial back. Use this when the child can reach the parent's network but the parent cannot reach the child — a common segmented-network shape. The tcp_rev_target is the parent's listener as reachable FROM THE CHILD, not from the operator workstation. The tcp_rev_token must match the parent's, byte for byte. Both builds must reference the same pivot_key_path. There is no lockout on repeated auth failures in the reverse direction — the parent tolerates bad attempts by design, because the parent is the long-lived side and a counter would let any peer on the network disable it.

linux_stager._comment: Linux stager. A ~4 MB first-stage implant that checks in, fetches a full agent from the server, verifies its ECDSA signature and SHA-256, decrypts it in memory, and executes it. stage_name is required and must match the payload file stem under payloads/ — 'full' for payloads/full.bin. transport_mode must be exactly 'http'; url must start with https://. The stager has no evasion code, no sleep mask, no non-HTTP transports, no WASM host, and no agent signing key.

windows_injectable._comment: Windows HTTPS beacon with `migrate <pid>` support. Requires Donut on the build host (or a vendored copy at beacon/bin/donut). The second build pass wraps the pass-1 PE and rebuilds with the shellcode embedded, adding roughly 13 MB to the final binary. `migrate --self` works without this flag; only foreign-process injection needs it. The injected child is a pass-1 beacon — it can run every verb including `migrate --self`, but `migrate <pid>` from the child refuses because its InjectorShellcodeB64 is empty.

windows_paranoid_cronos._comment: Windows-amd64 stealth build with the fiber-based cronos sleep mask. The paranoid profile sets cronos by default; the evasion block below makes the choice explicit so this file is self-documenting even if the profile's default changes. Requires target_os=windows and target_arch=amd64 — the builder refuses cronos on any other target with an error naming the mismatch. Every sleep cycle generates a fresh RC4 key, so two consecutive sleeps never produce the same ciphertext. The goroutine stack is NOT encrypted by this mask, because the Go runtime's signal handler walks the stack during the wait. Pick 'hwbp' instead if you need to avoid the fiber API calls; pick 'aes-ctr' if the target is not amd64 Windows.

linux_injectable._comment: Linux HTTPS beacon with `migrate <pid>` support. The second build pass prepends the vendored ELF-loader stub at beacon/bin/inject_linux_stub.bin to the pass-1 ELF and embeds the concatenation. Donut is not consulted on Linux — it emits PE loaders, not ELF loaders. Linux injection is x86-64 only; an arm64 build refuses the injection pass and produces a `migrate --self`-only binary.

windows_dll._comment: Windows DLL output. Uses -buildmode=c-shared, which requires a C compiler on PATH — gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64 for a Linux → Windows build, or MinGW-w64 / MSVC Build Tools for a Windows-native build. The DLL has no entry point to run the WebSocket loop, so transport_mode='websocket' is refused for this output format. Cannot be a stager. mTLS is supported.

windows_shellcode._comment: Windows shellcode output. Donut wraps the compiled PE in a position-independent loader that can be delivered through any shellcode-accepting vector — BOF, macro, PowerShell, DLL sideload, or a stager. Requires Donut on PATH or at beacon/bin/donut. amd64 and 386 only; Donut does not emit arm64. Compatible with `inject: true`.

_section_opsec: 1. OPSEC profile
Base evasion profile. Valid values: default, stealth, opsec,
paranoid. See beacon/builder.py:OPSEC_PROFILES for the exact
toggles each profile sets. Individual toggles under 'evasion'
override this one key at a time.
default    no evasion
stealth    string obfuscation
opsec      anti-sandbox, AMSI bypass, ETW patch, AES-CTR
sleep mask, indirect syscalls, string obfuscation,
garble, PPID spoof, anti-debug, anti-VM,
tls_profile='chrome'
paranoid   everything in opsec plus UPX, sleep mask='ekko',
ppid_spoof off, tls_profile='chrome'
IMPORTANT for output_format='stager':
The stager is a ~4 MB first-stage implant. It does not carry
any of the evasion features the full agent does. The
opsec_profile field is accepted by the loader for schema
consistency, but the stager's build path only reads a small
subset (verbose, url, kill_days, the C2 profile's paths and
headers, the server's ECDSA public key, and the root CA).
The rest is silently ignored — the flag is not emitted into
the stager binary because the stager has no code path to
honour it.
If the operator needs evasion, build a full agent and stage
it separately.
IMPORTANT for Linux targets:
amsi_bypass, etw_patch, and ppid_spoof are Windows-only and
are no-ops on a Linux target. The builder accepts them and
emits the linker flags; the agent has no code path to honour
them on a non-Windows host.
IMPORTANT for sleep_mask:
The sleep mask is set through the 'evasion' block below, under
the key 'evasion.sleep_mask'. The config file is the record of
the choice — a --sleep-mask flag on the command line overrides
it for one build, but a config-file build always reflects what
the file says. Keep the value in the config.
Valid values: 'none', 'rc4', 'aes-ctr', 'cronos', 'hwbp'.
The first four are accepted on both Linux and Windows except
that cronos is Windows-amd64 only. hwbp is Windows-amd64 only.
The builder refuses a Windows-only mask on a non-Windows target
or on an arm64 architecture, with an error naming the mismatch.
'ekko' is refused. It was reserved in earlier documentation for
a technique the framework never implemented. The builder names
'cronos' and 'hwbp' as the working alternatives.
The paranoid profile sets 'cronos'. A paranoid build for Linux
or arm64 is refused at build time; override with
sleep_mask='aes-ctr' in the evasion block for those targets.

_section_transport: 3. Transport
transport_mode      a comma-separated list of the failover-capable
transports (drawn from 'http', 'dns', 'doh',
'icmp'), or one of the single-transport
values 'smb', 'tcp', 'tcprev', 'quic',
'websocket', 'wireguard'.
http        HTTPS + JSON. Requires url. Applies the
c2_profile's paths, User-Agent, extra headers,
shaping block, per-shape encoding and placement,
per-role status codes, cookie name, and response
headers.
dns         UDP DNS TXT. Requires dns_domain. Reads only the
c2_profile's 'dns_label' block (verb characters
and per-chunk payload length).
doh         DNS-over-HTTPS to a public resolver. Requires
dns_domain; optionally doh_resolver. Blends with
browser DoH; escapes UDP/53 filters. Reads the
same 'dns_label' block as DNS. tls_profile
applies to the ClientHello to the public resolver.
icmp        ICMP echo transport. Linux only on both sides.
Requires icmp_host and CAP_NET_RAW on the C2 host.
quic        QUIC / HTTP/3 over UDP. Same C2 protocol as HTTP
on a different carriage; reaches networks that
permit HTTP/3 but block or proxy direct TCP.
Requires url; the url port must match the handler's
--beacon-quic-port. Cannot be combined with other
transports in this version. Needs aioquic on the
server and quic-go in the agent's go.mod.
websocket   WebSocket over TLS (wss://). One connection per
check-in cycle; the JSON body inside the frame is
identical to the HTTP transport's. Requires url;
the url port must match the handler's --ws-port.
The scheme is converted to wss:// at dial time by
the client. Cannot be combined with other
transports in this version. Needs simple-websocket
on the server and coder/websocket in the agent's
go.mod. mTLS is not supported.
wireguard   Kernel WireGuard on the server, userspace on the
agent. The C2 protocol runs over a private tunnel
IP; the outer transport is a WireGuard UDP stream.
Requires all four of wireguard_server_pubkey,
wireguard_server_addr, wireguard_agent_privkey,
wireguard_tunnel_ip. Cannot be combined with
other transports in this version. Needs pyroute2,
the wireguard kernel module, and CAP_NET_ADMIN
on the server; needs chrj/wgnet in the agent's
go.mod. Keypairs are distributed out of band, not
by the builder — see section 3b-iv below.
smb         Windows named-pipe pivot child. Requires
smb_pipe AND pivot_key_path. Cannot be combined
with other transports.
tcp         TCP pivot listener child. Requires tcp_bind_addr,
tcp_bind_token, AND pivot_key_path. Cannot be
combined with others.
tcprev      TCP reverse pivot child. Dials a TCP listener the
parent opened; the parent does NOT dial back. The
mirror image of 'tcp'. Requires tcp_rev_target,
tcp_rev_token, AND pivot_key_path. Cannot be
combined with others.
http,dns    HTTP primary, rotate to DNS after N failures.
http,doh    HTTP primary, rotate to DoH after N failures.
dns,doh     UDP DNS primary, rotate to DoH after N failures.
Rotation is a ring, not a preference list. Once the agent
rotates it stays on the new transport until that one also fails
N times. Session-level failures (expired cookie, forgotten
session) do not count toward the failover threshold; they are
fixed by a fresh check-in on the same transport.
transport_failover_after   Consecutive transport-level failures
before rotating. 0 disables rotation
entirely. Only meaningful on a
multi-transport list.
_section_http: 3a. HTTP fields (apply when 'http' is in transport_mode)
url           Callback URL. Must start with https:// — the
builder refuses a plaintext callback. Blank =
derive from the running handler.
For a WebSocket build, this field carries the
same value an HTTP build would use, but the port
must match the handler's --ws-port, NOT its
--beacon-port. The client converts https:// to
wss:// at dial time.
For a QUIC build, the port must match the
handler's --beacon-quic-port.
tls_profile   ClientHello fingerprint: 'go' | 'chrome' |
'firefox' | 'safari'. The presets are version-
pinned on purpose: a `go mod tidy` that pulls a
newer uTLS cannot silently change what the agent
looks like on the wire.
Applies to: HTTP, DoH, WebSocket.
Accepted but ignored: QUIC (composes its own
ClientHello, no uTLS dialer), WireGuard (inner
TLS uses the Go standard library).
c2_profile    Named profile under profiles/c2/. Controls the
HTTP fingerprint (User-Agent, linux_user_agent,
request paths, extra request headers, per-role
request headers) AND the malleable shaping block:
per-shape encoding ('base64' | 'base64url' |
'hex' | 'netbios'), per-shape placement (body |
response header | Set-Cookie), per-role HTTP
status codes ('status' block), the session cookie
name ('cookie_name'), additional response headers
merged onto every response ('response_headers'),
DNS verb characters and per-chunk payload length
(the 'dns_label' block, read by DNS and DoH
builds), and the stager's fetch path (the
'stager' block).
Thirty profiles ship in-tree: amazon,
apple-icloud, aws-s3, azure-blob, chrome,
cloudflare, discord, dns, dropbox, github,
gitlab, google-analytics, google-drive,
instagram, jira, linkedin, notion, o365, okta,
onedrive, salesforce, shopify, slack, spotify,
stripe, teams, telegram, webex, youtube, zoom.
The 'dns' profile is a special case: it declares
only a 'dns_label' block and is intended for
'--transport dns' or '--transport doh' builds.
Two operational notes on profile selection:
· Pair the C2 profile with a matching
tls_profile. A profile that claims Chrome
while the ClientHello is the Go standard
library is a two-signal mismatch.
· Pick the profile whose presence is boring on
the target's egress path. A consumer-
application profile on a consumer network is
unremarkable; on an OT segment it is the
loudest thing on the wire.
_section_websocket: 3a-ii. WebSocket fields
(apply only when 'websocket' is in transport_mode)
The WebSocket transport reuses the HTTP transport's url field.
There is no separate WebSocket URL field — the same callback
address an HTTP beacon would use is used here, and the client
converts the https:// scheme to wss:// at dial time.
The url port must match the handler's --ws-port, NOT the
--beacon-port the HTTP listener is bound to. The handler
binds a second TLS socket on that port alongside its HTTP
listener; it reuses the same certificate and CA material.
For example, if the handler runs with --beacon-port 8881 and
--ws-port 8884, a WebSocket build's url field is
https://c2.example.com:8884 — the 8884, not the 8881.
tls_profile applies: the WebSocket handshake is a real TLS
handshake and the ClientHello is the fingerprint that matters.
The c2_profile applies too: paths, User-Agent, and extra
headers travel on the WebSocket upgrade request exactly as
they would on an HTTPS GET.
The default WebSocket path is /ws, which the C2 profile's
beacon_path overrides when one is set.
Cannot be combined with other transports in this version.
mTLS is not supported — simple-websocket does not expose the
peer certificate after the handshake.

_section_wireguard: 3b-iv. WireGuard fields
(apply only when 'wireguard' is in transport_mode)
Unlike every other transport, the WireGuard keypairs are not
generated by the builder. The server generates its own keypair
on first run and prints the public half at startup:
[BEACON] WireGuard listener on UDP 51820
[BEACON] server pubkey: <base64>
The operator generates an agent keypair out of band on the
team server:
wg genkey | tee agent.key | wg pubkey
The private half goes into this build. The public half is
pinned on the running handler after the agent is deployed,
from the local console:
beacon> wireguard add-peer <agent-pubkey> 10.99.0.2
Until the pin is in place the server's WireGuard device
silently drops the agent's packets — WireGuard does not accept
traffic from an unknown peer. This is the same trust-on-first-
use model as the check-in path: the operator decides which
peer public key is legitimate.
Requirements:
· pyroute2 on the server (pip install pyroute2)
· The `wireguard` kernel module loaded (`modprobe wireguard`)
· wireguard-tools on PATH for the one-time server keypair
generation on first launch (the `wg` command). Not required
after .keys/wireguard/server.key exists.
· CAP_NET_ADMIN on the Python process on the C2 host:
sudo setcap cap_net_admin+ep $(which python3)
or run the handler as root
· chrj/wgnet in the agent's go.mod
Three tunnel addresses and two ports, easy to conflate:
wireguard_server_addr       The server's OUTER UDP listener
as host:port (default 51820).
This is where the agent's
userspace WireGuard stack sends
handshake packets.
wireguard_tunnel_ip         The AGENT's own IPv4 address
inside the tunnel. 10.99.0.2 for
the first agent; increment per
agent.
wireguard_server_tunnel_ip  The SERVER's IPv4 address inside
the tunnel (default 10.99.0.1).
Must match the handler's
--wireguard-server-ip. A handler
started with a non-default value
needs every agent rebuilt with
the matching field set — otherwise
the agent dials an address that
does not exist on the tunnel, with
the same silent-failure symptom as
an unpinned peer.
wireguard_inner_port        The INNER HTTPS port the agent
dials on the server's tunnel IP
(default 8881). Must match the
handler's --beacon-port. Distinct
from the port in
wireguard_server_addr — that
value carries the outer WireGuard
UDP port, which has nothing to do
with the inner HTTPS listener.
The server side does not need a second listener bound to the
tunnel IP. The outer HTTP listener already binds 0.0.0.0 on the
beacon port, so it accepts traffic arriving through the
WireGuard interface. Running a second listener on
10.99.0.1:8881 would collide with the outer one (EADDRINUSE).
The C2 profile applies to the INNER HTTPS request — paths,
User-Agent, extra headers, shaping, per-shape encoding and
placement, per-role status codes, cookie name, and response
headers all travel through the tunnel and are processed by the
listener on the far side. The one thing the profile cannot
control is the OUTER WireGuard handshake: the message-type
bytes, handshake timing, fixed-length keys, and outer UDP port
are set by the WireGuard protocol and by the wireguard_* build
flags, not by the profile. tls_profile does NOT apply to the
inner TLS handshake — the inner connection uses the Go standard
library's crypto/tls, not uTLS. The inner TLS never crosses the
public wire, so the missing uTLS profile is invisible to
anything outside the tunnel.
Cannot be combined with other transports in this version.
_section_pivot: 3c. SMB and TCP pivot keypair (SMB and TCP only)
Every SMB and TCP build — parent or child, in any combination
— reads the same engagement-wide pivot keypair file at compile
time. The builder embeds the half the build's role needs:
parent  (smb_relay_pipe or tcp_relay_target is set)
→ embeds the PRIVATE half, used to sign the pivot
handshake's AckMsg and to derive the ECDH shared
secret with each connecting child
child   (transport_mode is 'smb' or 'tcp')
→ embeds the PUBLIC half, used to verify the
parent's AckMsg against the pinned pivot key
both    (a pivot child that also relays for a deeper child)
→ embeds both halves. Legal, and both the SMB child
transport and the SMB parent listener read the
half they need from the same keypair.
The value is a path on the TEAM SERVER, not the operator
workstation — the compile happens on the server, and the file
is read there. A remote build's pivot_key_path is validated
against the same whitelist as mTLS material: the value must
resolve under mtls_certs/, tls_certs/, or profiles/c2/. The
recommended location is mtls_certs/pivot.pem.
Generate the file once per engagement with:
beacon-build --pivot-key-gen mtls_certs/pivot.pem
on the local console. The file contains both halves of an
ECDSA P-256 keypair as PEM (a PRIVATE KEY block and a PUBLIC
KEY block). It is written 0600.
The private half is a single point of compromise for the
parent-to-child hop. An attacker who recovers it from a parent
binary can impersonate a pivot listener to any pivot client,
but cannot decrypt the child's C2 traffic to the team server
— that requires the server ECDH key. Treat the file with the
same care as a CA key: back it up, do not commit it, and
rotate it only when the whole deployment is being rebuilt.
FORWARD SECRECY. The pivot handshake does NOT provide forward
secrecy. The parent's ECDH contribution is derived from its
static pivot key; only the child contributes a fresh
ephemeral. An attacker who recovers the pivot private key
from a captured parent binary can derive the session keys for
any past pivot session whose ciphertext AND child ephemeral
public key they captured. The server-ECDH layer on the
child's own C2 envelope is independent and does provide
forward secrecy across check-ins; the pivot tunnel does not.
On a deployment where captured ciphertext is part of the
threat model, rotate the pivot keypair per engagement, and
treat the private half as an engagement-lifetime secret.
Rotating the file requires rebuilding every parent AND every
child. There is no backward compatibility and no negotiated
fallback.
Wire encryption (server_ecdh_pubkey_b64) IS supported on SMB
and TCP pivot children — the child's C2 envelope travels inside
the AEAD-encrypted pivot session and is never visible to the
parent. This is the opposite of the old transparent-relay
model, where wire encryption was refused on SMB and TCP
children.
_section_smb: 3d. SMB named-pipe transport (Windows only)
smb_pipe makes this agent a child (dials a parent).
smb_relay_pipe makes this agent a parent (listens for
children). The relay side is orthogonal to the parent's own
transport — a parent on http or dns can relay at the same
time.
smb_pipe accepts three forms:
bare name    'tornado_relay_001'
→ \\.\pipe\tornado_relay_001
Same-host pivot: the child and parent run on the
SAME Windows host. The child opens a local pipe.
local path   '\\.\pipe\tornado_relay_001'
Identical behaviour to a bare name.
UNC path     '\\WIN-SRV2\pipe\tornado_relay_001'
Cross-host pivot: the child opens a pipe on
WIN-SRV2 over SMB. Requires:
· WIN-SRV2 resolvable from the child (DNS,
NetBIOS, or hosts file — or use an IP
directly: '\\10.0.0.5\pipe\name')
· TCP/445 reachable from the child to the
parent
· the child's process token able to
authenticate to WIN-SRV2 (domain user, or
matching local credentials)
On bash, single-quote the value so the shell
does not collapse the leading double backslash.
On cmd.exe, double every backslash.
Every SMB build, parent or child, also needs pivot_key_path.
The parent creates a named pipe with the default security
descriptor, so any process that can reach the pipe's host over
SMB with credentials the host's default policy accepts is
admitted to the handshake. The pivot session's AEAD layer and
the child's identity signature are what stop a wrong-
credentialed client from being trusted as a legitimate child.
The parent's smb_relay_pipe must be a local pipe name or a
\\.\pipe\ path, NOT a UNC path. Windows publishes the
parent's local pipe to the SMB layer automatically; there is
no reason to name the parent's pipe with a UNC prefix.

_section_tcprev: 3f. TCP pivot transport — reverse direction
The 'tcprev' transport is the mirror image of 'tcp': the parent
opens a listener and the child dials out. Use it when the child
can reach the parent's network but the parent cannot reach the
child — a common shape on segmented networks where a jump host
has bidirectional access but the parent sits behind a NAT or
firewall.
Generate a token on the parent with --tcp-rev-token-gen or the
same secrets.token_hex(32) command. The token must be 64 hex
characters (32 bytes), and both ends must carry the same value.
Two roles, two sets of fields:
parent (tcp_rev_listen is set; the parent listens)
→ tcp_rev_listen, tcp_rev_token
child  (transport_mode='tcprev'; the child dials out)
→ tcp_rev_target, tcp_rev_token
Unlike the bind direction, the parent does NOT lock out on
repeated authentication failures. The parent is the long-lived
side and a persistent counter would let any peer on the
network disable the listener with three bad attempts. The
child is the one that would have to redeploy to recover, and
on a segmented network that recovery is not always possible.
The 'tcp' and 'tcprev' transports are NOT interchangeable. A
'tcp' child listens; a 'tcprev' parent listens; neither
dials. A 'tcp' child cannot connect to a 'tcprev' parent —
rebuild with the matching transport on both sides before
deploying.
Every tcprev build, parent or child, also needs pivot_key_path.

_section_inject: 4b. In-memory injection
inject (bool, default false) — runs a second build pass that
embeds a loader-wrapped copy of the pass-1 binary as base64 in
the agent's linker flags, then rebuilds. The resulting binary
can `migrate <pid>` into any process the beacon has permission
to open. Costs roughly 13 MB of final binary size for a typical
Go beacon.
Two platform paths, dispatched inside the builder:
Windows  the builder runs Donut on the pass-1 PE and embeds
the resulting shellcode. Requires `donut` on PATH
on the build host, or a vendored copy at
beacon/bin/donut. Refused for output_format 'dll'
and 'stager' — a DLL or a stager cannot inject
itself.
Linux    the builder prepends the vendored ELF-loader stub
at beacon/bin/inject_linux_stub.bin to the pass-1
ELF and embeds the concatenation. Requires that
stub file to exist; if it does not, the build
prints a warning and produces a binary that
supports `migrate --self` only. Refused for
output_format other than 'elf'. Linux injection is
x86-64 only; an arm64 build refuses the injection
pass.
Other    refused at build time. The runtime injection paths
are Linux and Windows only.
`migrate --self` works with or without this flag. Only the
foreign-process form (`migrate <pid>` / `migrate <name>`) needs
the embedded shellcode.
The two-pass build produces a shipped binary whose injected
child is a pass-1 beacon — it can run every verb including
`migrate --self`, but `migrate <pid>` from the child refuses,
because its InjectorShellcodeB64 is empty. If you need chain
injection, inject from the parent.
_section_stager: 5. Stager fields (only when output_format='stager')
The stager checks in, fetches the full agent under payloads/
from the server, verifies its signature and SHA-256, decrypts
it, and executes it in memory.
stage_name       Required. Payload stem the server serves, e.g.
'full' for payloads/full.bin. The AES key is
recorded in payloads/stage_keys.json under this
name so the server can find it.
stage_key_hex    Optional. 32-byte AES-256-GCM key, hex-encoded.
Blank = generate a fresh key per build.
Constraints enforced by the builder:
· transport_mode must be exactly 'http'
· url must start with https://
· mTLS is not supported on stagers
· output_format 'dll' is refused
· inject must be false
Defaults that apply unless the build overrides them:
· work_hours_start / work_hours_end — inherited from the
same fields the full agent reads, so a config that sets
the window for a full agent also gates the stager.
· server_ecdh_pubkey_b64 — always the handler's running
ECDH key, the same as a full-agent build. A stager built
by a handler with no working `cryptography` package falls
back to plaintext, matching the pre-wire-encryption
posture.
What the stager DOES do:
· verify the handler's ECDSA signature on every served payload
· verify the ECDSA signature on every stage_load task
· verify the SHA-256 of the decrypted payload
· respect the work_hours_start / work_hours_end window the
full agent respects. Outside the window the stager sleeps
without contacting the server.
· encrypt every request body with the same AES-256-GCM
envelope the full agent uses, when the build embeds a
ServerECDHPubkey.
· unwrap a check-in or tasks response when the listener's
C2 profile has a shaping block, and wrap a result post
when the profile has a results_request block.
What the stager does NOT do (deliberately):
- carry any evasion code (AMSI, ETW, PPID, anti-VM, ...)
- carry the sleep mask
- carry DoH, ICMP, WebSocket, WireGuard, SMB, or TCP
transport code
- carry the WASM extension host
- carry an identity signature (the stager has no agent
signing key; the server treats its check-in as TOFU)
_section_evasion: 6. Evasion overrides
Per-key overrides applied on top of opsec_profile. Delete the
whole block to inherit the profile unchanged. Values below are
the 'default' profile; the wizard writes whichever profile was
picked.
sleep_mask       Sleep-obfuscation mode. Set through the config
file; the --sleep-mask flag on the command line
is an override for scripted builds, not the
primary interface. Valid values:
'none'       No mask. The beacon sleeps for the full interval
with nothing encrypted. Labs and diagnostics only.
'rc4'        Encrypts the executable segment with a per-cycle
RC4 key during the wait, via a native sleep stub
that does not enter the Go runtime. Linux and
Windows. The mask excludes a fixed tail of the
segment so the stub stays executable; the runtime
refuses the build if the linker places the stub
outside that tail, and names the function and the
tail bounds in the error.
'aes-ctr'    Same mechanism as rc4, AES-256-CTR cipher. Linux
and Windows. The default in every OPSEC profile
that enables a mask.
'cronos'     Windows-amd64 only. Fiber-based: the calling
thread becomes a fiber, a second encrypt fiber
runs the wait with the image and the primary
fiber's stack region encrypted, then control
returns to the primary fiber with everything
decrypted. No timer, no APC, no new kernel-
visible thread. The Windows detection surface is
the fiber API calls themselves, which are not
hooked by the EDR rules that watch for the Ekko
and Foliage artifacts.
'hwbp'       Windows-amd64 only. A debug-register breakpoint
on NtWaitForSingleObject raises a #DB before the
wait begins. A native Vectored Exception Handler
encrypts, performs the wait via a direct syscall,
decrypts, and adjusts RIP past the breakpoint.
No timer, no APC, no fiber, no new thread. Higher
EDR signal than cronos because DR0 and DR7 are
individually observable, so this is not the
default for any profile — pick it explicitly.
'ekko'       Not accepted. Reserved in earlier documentation
for a technique the framework never implemented.
A build that names it is refused with a message
pointing at 'cronos' or 'hwbp'.
Platform coverage:
Linux    rc4, aes-ctr
Windows  rc4, aes-ctr, cronos, hwbp (all amd64 only except
rc4 and aes-ctr, which also work on arm64)
Every mode generates a fresh key on every sleep cycle, so two
consecutive sleeps never produce the same ciphertext.
What the mask does NOT encrypt: the goroutine stack. The Go
runtime may be preempted by an async signal during the wait,
and its signal handler walks the stack. Encrypting a stack
the handler needs to walk crashes the process. This is the
same limitation every sleep-mask design that runs on the Go
runtime has.
syscall_method   'direct' | 'indirect'
garble           Requires garble on PATH on the build host.
Installed automatically by install-go-build.sh
at a pinned version.
upx              Requires upx on PATH. UPX markers are
signatured by some EDRs — disable for those
engagements.
verbose          Writes diagnostic stderr on the target.
Debug builds only; never enable on a live op.
amsi_bypass, etw_patch, and ppid_spoof are Windows-only and
are no-ops on a Linux target. The builder accepts them and
emits the linker flags; the agent has no code path to honour
them on a non-Windows host.
sleep_mask='cronos' and sleep_mask='hwbp' are also Windows-only,
and Windows-amd64-only on top of that. The builder refuses either
one on a non-Windows target, on arm64, or on 386 — no binary is
emitted. Use 'aes-ctr' or 'rc4' for Linux, arm64, or 386.
antivm and antisanbox are aggressive. When a beacon built with
these flags runs inside a VM, it exits silently. Test builds
on virtualised infrastructure must disable them.

_section_notes: 8. Notes on fields that live outside this file
A few BeaconBuildConfig fields are set by the handler before it
calls the builder, not by the JSON config. They are listed here
for reference only; they are not settable from a build config.
agent_keypair_path       Path to the agent's build-time ECDSA
P-256 signing key. If empty, a fresh
keypair is generated per build, and
redeploying over an existing session
is rejected by the server as an
impersonation attempt. Set to a stable
file to make rebuilds idempotent.
server_ecdh_pubkey_b64   The handler's running wire-encryption
public key. Embedded automatically
when the handler has a working
`cryptography` package.
server_pubkey_path       Path to the handler's task-signing
public key. Embedded in stager
builds so the stager can verify
payload signatures. If the handler
has no working ECDSA signer, this is
not staged and the stager is built
with signature verification off —
the builder prints a warning in that
case.
injector_shellcode_b64   Set internally by the second build
pass. Never set this from a config;
the builder overwrites it.
client_cert_path,        Populated by the handler when an
client_key_path,         mTLS bundle is embedded. The JSON
root_ca_path             'mtls' block is the operator-facing
interface; these are the resolved
